title: Resi4Rent — Art Direction
desc: Two years of art direction that refuses to become wallpaper

blocks.title: Resi4Rent — Art Direction
blocks.lede: Fifty-plus pieces. Two years. One visual system built to keep rental marketing from becoming wallpaper.

items.label: Role
items.value: Art direction, campaign system, ongoing creative direction

items.label: Scope
items.value: Campaign concept, composition/type system, outdoor, digital, mobile, illustration, ongoing content

items.statement: Real-estate marketing has a wallpaper problem.
body: Smiling stock photography. Predictable layouts. The same promise repeated with a different logo.
Resi4Rent already had a strong brand. What it needed was a way to make the marketing feel more human without losing consistency.

items.statement: Build the system before building the assets.
body: The first launch had to work on citylights, A-frames and digital screens — three formats with completely different reading conditions. I built fixed rules for composition and typography, then let the content change inside them.

Once that structure was in place, the brief became bigger than “units available”. The work could start talking about what choosing a home actually feels like: comfort, routine, daily rituals, the emotional logic of a place.

blocks.text: One system. The same character on the street and on a phone.

body: The launch campaign, adaptation rules and more than 50 pieces of output across posters, animations, billboards, events and internal communication.
Some executions are bold and illustrative. Others are quieter and lifestyle-led. They vary without drifting.

blocks.statement: That is the real test of a creative system: whether it keeps working when the original designer isn’t in the room.
body: The framework became useful beyond the original campaign. The internal team was able to extend the system into new formats independently.
